\chapter{Once More, Please}
\label{ch:hi-once-more-please}
\hlchaptermodality{110}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can ask someone to say it again or louder, to wait a minute, and what something means.}

Complete HI-C110-matlab: keep a conversation going when you cannot follow it.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[dobārā]{\hi{दोबारा} (dobārā) — again, a second time}

\label{lesson:HI-C110-dobara}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for alone, then the Hindi for cold.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{दोबारा}}
\textbf{\hi{दोबारा}} (\emph{dobārā}) — \textquotedblleft{}again, a second time\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\hi{दोबारा} \hi{बोलिए}} — \textquotedblleft{}please say it again\textquotedblright{}. It is \textbf{\hi{दो}}, \textquotedblleft{}two\textquotedblright{}, and \textbf{\hi{बार}}, \textquotedblleft{}a time\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The repair a beginner needs most.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dobārā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dobārā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{dobārā bolie}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for alone, then the Hindi for cold, then say \emph{dobārā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{दोबारा} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Again, a second time\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[zor se]{\hi{ज़ोर} \hi{से} (zor se) — loudly}

\label{lesson:HI-C110-zorse}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for cold, then the Hindi for again.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{ज़ोर} \hi{से}}
\textbf{\hi{ज़ोर} \hi{से}} (\emph{zor se}) — \textquotedblleft{}loudly\textquotedblright{}, literally \textquotedblleft{}with force\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\hi{थोड़ा} \hi{ज़ोर} \hi{से} \hi{बोलिए}} — \textquotedblleft{}please speak a little louder\textquotedblright{}, with the softening \textbf{\hi{थोड़ा}}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Again, and louder.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{zor se}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{zor se}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{thoṛā zor se bolie}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for cold, then the Hindi for again, then say \emph{zor se} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{ज़ोर} \hi{से} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Loudly\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[ek minaṭ]{\hi{एक} \hi{मिनट} (ek minaṭ) — one minute, a moment}

\label{lesson:HI-C110-ekminat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for again, then the Hindi for loudly.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{एक} \hi{मिनट}}
\textbf{\hi{एक} \hi{मिनट}} (\emph{ek minaṭ}) — \textquotedblleft{}one minute\textquotedblright{}, said the way English says \textquotedblleft{}a moment\textquotedblright{}.

English \emph{minute}, borrowed, after the \textbf{\hi{एक}} you count with.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A way to buy time while you find the word.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ek minaṭ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ek minaṭ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{ek minaṭ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for again, then the Hindi for loudly, then say \emph{ek minaṭ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{एक} \hi{मिनट} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}One minute, a moment\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[rukie]{\hi{रुकिए} (rukie) — please wait, please stop}

\label{lesson:HI-C110-rukie}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for loudly, then the Hindi for one minute.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{रुकिए}}
\textbf{\hi{रुकिए}} (\emph{rukie}) — \textquotedblleft{}please wait\textquotedblright{}, \textquotedblleft{}please stop\textquotedblright{}.

It is \textbf{\hi{रुकना}}, \textquotedblleft{}to stop\textquotedblright{}, with the respectful ending of \textbf{\hi{बोलिए}}. \textbf{\hi{रुकिए}, \hi{एक} \hi{मिनट}} — \textquotedblleft{}wait, one minute\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Wait, one minute, again, louder.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rukie}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rukie}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{rukie, ek minaṭ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for loudly, then the Hindi for one minute, then say \emph{rukie} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{रुकिए} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Please wait, please stop\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[matlab]{\hi{मतलब} (matlab) — meaning}

\label{lesson:HI-C110-matlab}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for one minute, then the Hindi for please wait.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{मतलब}}
\textbf{\hi{मतलब}} (\emph{matlab}) — \textquotedblleft{}meaning\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\hi{धीरे} \hi{का} \hi{मतलब} \hi{क्या} \hi{है}?} — \textquotedblleft{}what does \emph{dhīre} mean?\textquotedblright{}. Put any word in front of \textbf{\hi{का} \hi{मतलब} \hi{क्या} \hi{है}?} and it becomes the question that turns any speaker into a teacher.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Again, louder, one minute, wait, what does it mean.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{matlab}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{matlab}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} ask \emph{dhīre kā matlab kyā hai?}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for one minute, then the Hindi for please wait, then say \emph{matlab} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{मतलब} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Meaning\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
